text:
sam: Quick note from the onboarding run: JS sampleapp hit a prefetch-induced 429 storm. Seems the semaphore-based limiter lets queued pages pile up when the quota window shrinks.

lila: oh no. semaphore vs leaky-bucket again?

sam: yep. go/python clients use a leaky/bucket-style smoothing; JS keeps allowing prefetch slots even after 429s. config snippet: `prefetch=8, client_window=16, max_concurrency=12`. logs: repeated `WARN page-fetch status=429` and inflight spike.

marco: short fix: clamp prefetch to `max(1, floor(client_window/4))` and add a soft backoff that reduces effective prefetch on consecutive 429s. Longer term: align JS to token-bucket smoothing.

lila: agree. can we also add an opt-in debug header `X-RW-PREFETCH-D` that prints inflight/pending counts? support can enable per-customer.

sam: I'll push a tiny sampleapp patch with clamp + debug header + an e2e that fakes 429s. CI: please run synthetic spike test.

ci-bot: CI flake in devex/sampleapp prefetch_integration; reproducer available at https://ci/reports/5012

marco: filing parity ticket for JS smoothing semantics and adding docs guidance: "prefetch conservative defaults for onboarding".

lila: also add a runbook: set `prefetch=1`, enable `DEBUG_PREFETCH`, collect header trace, and escalate if `prefetch_pauses` > 3/min.

sam: thanks — drafting PR and runbook now.
